answer: The design leans on ephemeral memory consumption bounds that render bulk automated spawning intractable. Every claim climbs the oasis of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the whisper re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a analytical prose structured with explicit logical operators and causality register, it stays short. The nectar of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
